column3: Then one should give the Supreme Self a bath with pure water while reciting the Pauruṣa, Vaiṣṇava, and Ghārma hymns and the three groups beginning with “pavasva.”

column2: ya indror ekavargaś ca samudrād ūrmir eva ca | jitanta iti stotraṃ ca paṭhan saṃsnāpayed dharim ||
column3: One should thoroughly bathe Hari while reciting the single group beginning “ya indra,” the hymn beginning “samudrād ūrmiḥ,” and the stotra beginning “jitante.”

column2: tato’ṅgamārjanaṃ vastraṃ pītaṃ ca paridhānakam | tataḥ sarvāṅgabhūṣāś ca nūpurādyāḥ kirīṭakam ||
column3: Then one should dry the limbs, offer a yellow garment for wearing, and afterward offer ornaments for every limb, beginning with anklets and extending to the crown.

column2: dhyātvaiva bhūṣaṇaṃ kiñcin navam apy arpayet sudhīḥ | yajñopavītaṃ dattvā tam āsane copaveśayet ||
column3: The wise worshipper should mentally fashion and offer any ornament that is not physically available; after giving the sacred thread, one should seat Him upon the throne.

column2: abhiṣekāt purā vāpi paścād vā paramātmani | tattvanyāsādi dhyānāntaṃ kṛtvā pūjāṃ samācaret ||
column3: Either before or after the ablution, one should perform upon the Supreme Self the sequence beginning with placement of the principles and ending with meditation, and then conduct the worship.

column2: āsanasthaṃ hariṃ spṛṣṭvā mūladvādaśakaṃ japet | arpayet gandhapuṣpāṇi mūlena tulasīṃ tathā ||
column3: Touching Hari seated upon the throne, one should recite the root mantra twelve times and, with that mantra, offer sandal paste, flowers, and tulasī.

column2: tataś cakrāyudhādīni pūjayet kramaśo daśa | durgā cakrādhidevī syāc chrīś ca śaṅkhādhidevatā ||
column3: Then one should worship in order the ten weapons beginning with the discus. Durgā is the presiding deity of the discus, and Śrī is the presiding deity of the conch.

column2: vāyur gadādhidevaḥ syād bhūmiḥ padmābhimāninī | durgaiva khaḍgadevī syāc chārṅgaṃ caiva sarasvatī ||
column3: Vāyu is the presiding deity of the mace; Earth identifies with the lotus; Durgā herself is the deity of the sword; and Sarasvatī identifies with Śārṅga, the bow.

column2: pañcaprāṇāḥ pañcabāṇā viriñcaḥ kaustubhātmakaḥ | śrīr eva vanamālāyāṃ lakṣmīḥ śrīvatsasaṃsthitā ||
column3: The five vital airs are the five arrows; Viriñca is present in the Kaustubha; Śrī herself is present in the forest garland; and Lakṣmī abides in the Śrīvatsa.

column2: athāvaraṇapūjāyāṃ lakṣmīṃ vāme harer yajet | dharāṃ ca dakṣiṇe pārśve tataḥ pūrvādidiṣu ca ||
column3: Next, in the worship of the enclosures, one should worship Lakṣmī on Hari’s left and Earth on His right, and then worship in the directions beginning with the east.

column2: kruddholkāya maholkāya vīrolkāya namas tataḥ | dyūlkāya ca namaskuryād udīcyāṃ diśi ca kramāt ||
column3: One should successively offer obeisance to Kruddholka, Maholka, Vīrolka, and Dyūlka, the last being in the northern direction.

column2: sahasrolkāyeti catur āgneyādividiṣu ca | punaḥ pūrvādikāṣṭāsu vāsudevādikān yajet ||
column3: The four forms beginning with Sahasrolka should be worshipped in the intermediate directions beginning with the southeast; then, in the eight directions beginning with the east, one should worship Vāsudeva and the succeeding forms.

column2: māyāṃ jayāṃ kṛtiṃ śāntiṃ yajet koṇeṣu ca kramāt | keśavādyās tato mūrtīr dvādaśa kramato yajet ||
column3: In the corner directions one should worship Māyā, Jayā, Kṛti, and Śānti in order; then one should worship in order the twelve forms beginning with Keśava.

column2: diśi dve dve koṇa eka aiśe dāmodaro bhavet | saṅkarṣaṇādikṛṣṇāntā mūrtayo dvādaśa kramāt ||
column3: There are two forms in each principal direction and one in each corner, with Dāmodara in the northeast; then come, in order, the twelve forms beginning with Saṅkarṣaṇa and ending with Kṛṣṇa.

column2: matsyādimūrtayo’nte dvādaśāntaṃ kramād yajet | aiśānyāṃ viśvarūpaḥ syāt krameṇānena pūjayet ||
column3: Finally one should worship in order the twelve forms beginning with Matsya; Viśvarūpa is in the northeast. They should be worshipped in this sequence.

column2: sarvadiṣu punaś cāpi hy anantādīn sabhāryakān | indrādīṃś ca sapatnīkān parigrahayutān api ||
column3: Again, in all the directions, one should worship Ananta and the others together with their consorts, and Indra and the other guardians together with their wives and entourages.

column2: pūjayet kramaśo dhīmān svāsu dikṣu sthitān bahiḥ | paścāt purastāc cheṣaṃ ca vidhiṃ caiva sabhāryakam ||
column3: The wise person should worship them successively outside, each in his own direction; afterward one should worship Śeṣa in the west and Vidhi in the east, each with his consort.

column2: pūjayitvā tataḥ pūjyā dvādaśa dvārapālakāḥ | prathamo vajranābhaś ca harīśaś ca tataḥ param ||
column3: After completing those worships, the twelve door guardians are to be worshipped: the first is Vajranābha, followed by Harīśa.

column2: tṛtīyo gāṅgatanayas tataḥ śaṅkhanidhīśvaraḥ | jayaś ca vijayaḥ paścād dhātā saptamako mataḥ ||
column3: The third is the son of Gaṅgā, followed by Śaṅkhanidhīśvara; next are Jaya and Vijaya, and Dhātā is regarded as the seventh.

column2: vidhātā ca tato bhadraḥ subhadro’thāmṛteśvaraḥ | virūpākṣo’ntimaś caiva namaḥśabdena pūjayet ||
column3: Then come Vidhātā, Bhadra, Subhadra, Amṛteśvara, and finally Virūpākṣa. Each should be worshipped with the word “namaḥ.”

column2: vanaspatyudbhavetyādi mantrair mūlapurassaraiḥ | dhūpaṃ dattvā tato dīpaṃ dadyān mūlam udīrayan ||
column3: With the mantras beginning “vanaspatyudbhava,” each preceded by the root mantra, one should offer incense; then, uttering the root mantra, one should offer the lamp.

column2: sājyaṃ trivartimantreṇa tato naivedyam arpayet | devasyāgre bhuvaṃ śodhya śrībījaṃ tatra saṃlikhet ||
column3: Using the mantra for the three-wicked lamp supplied with ghee, one should then offer the food. After purifying the ground before the deity, one should inscribe the seed syllable of Śrī there.

column2: naivedyam upari sthāpya śuddhatoyena prokṣayet | sauvarṇair iti mantreṇa mūlamantreṇa mantrayet ||
column3: One should place the food offering upon it, sprinkle it with pure water, and consecrate it with the mantra beginning “sauvarṇaiḥ” and with the root mantra.

column2: amṛtasrāviṇīṃ dhenuṃ naivedyopari cintayet | dhenumudrāṃ pradarśyoccaiḥ surabhyai nama ity api ||
column3: Above the food one should visualize a cow streaming nectar, display the Dhenu mudrā, and also say aloud, “Obeisance to Surabhi.”

column2: huṃ phaḍantaṃ saha svāhety uktvā mudrāṃ sudarśanīm | gāruḍīṃ cātha sandarśya gṛhītvātha kare jalam ||
column3: After uttering the formula ending in “huṃ phaṭ” together with “svāhā,” one should display the Sudarśana and Gāruḍī mudrās and then take water in the hand.

column2: pariṣiñcāmi satyaṃ tv arteneti ca kramād vadet | paritaḥ siñcayet toyaṃ tata āpośanaṃ kṣipet ||
column3: One should say in order, “I sprinkle around” and “You are truth, through sacred order,” sprinkle water all around, and then offer the water for āpośana.

column2: mahālakṣmyā sudhārūpaṃ kare te dakṣiṇe’nagha | āpośanaṃ dīyamānaṃ piba deva ramāpate ||
column3: “O sinless Lord of Ramā, drink the āpośana, nectar in form, that Mahālakṣmī offers into Your right hand.”

column2: sudhārasaṃ suvipulam āpośanam idaṃ tava | gṛhāṇa tvaṃ suraśreṣṭha yatheṣṭam upabhujyatām ||
column3: “This abundant āpośana is the essence of nectar for You. Accept it, O best of the gods, and partake of it as You desire.”

column2: iti mantram udīryātha devadakṣiṇahastake | lakṣmyā pradīyamānaṃ ca sudhārasamayaṃ śubham ||
column3: Having uttered this mantra, one should visualize the auspicious substance made of nectar being offered by Lakṣmī into the deity’s right hand—

column2: āpośanam idaṃ dhyātvāmṛtopastaraṇam asi | ity uktvāpośanocchiṣṭajalaṃ pātrāntare kṣipet ||
column3: —meditating upon it as this āpośana. Saying, “You are the spreading of nectar,” one should pour the remaining āpośana water into another vessel.

column2: tataḥ prāṇātmane pūrvam uktvā nārāyaṇāya ca | svāhāntam iti pañcaitā āhutīḥ kramaśo vadan ||
column3: Then one should first name Prāṇātman and Nārāyaṇa, ending each formula with “svāhā,” and utter the five offerings in sequence.

column2: śaṅkhatoyaṃ kṣipet pātre pratyāhuty ekapātrakam | madhuvātā tathā svādu bhojaṃ tveti paṭhed ṛcaḥ ||
column3: For each offering one should place conch water into the appropriate vessel; then one should recite the ṛks beginning “madhu vātā,” “svādu,” and “bhojaṃ tvā.”

column2: pānīyam arpayet paścāt tato javanikāṃ kṣipet | bhuñjānaṃ cintayen mūlaṃ japed aṣṭottaraṃ śatam ||
column3: Afterward one should offer drinking water and then draw the curtain; while visualizing the Lord eating, one should recite the root mantra 108 times.

column2: uttarāpośanaṃ paścād amṛtāpidhānam asi | ity uktvāpośanocchiṣṭajalaṃ pātrāntare kṣipet ||
column3: Next comes the concluding āpośana. Saying, “You are the covering of nectar,” one should pour the remaining āpośana water into another vessel.

column2: vāme gaṇḍūṣapātraṃ syāt tatra gaṇḍūṣam arpayet | hastaprakṣālanaṃ tatra paścād ācamanam kṣipet | mūlena puṣpatritayam arpayitvā tato vadet ||
column3: The vessel for rinsing the mouth should be on the left; there one should offer the mouth-rinse, then water for washing the hands, and afterward water for sipping. Having offered three flowers with the root mantra, one should then say:

column2: pūgīphalaṃ sakhadirajīrṇakarpūrasaṃyutam | nāgavallīdalair yuktaṃ tāmbūlaṃ gṛhyatāṃ vibho | iti tāmbūlakaṃ dadyān nākasyeti ca dakṣiṇām ||
column3: “O all-pervading Lord, accept this tāmbūla consisting of areca nut, khadira, jīrṇaka, and camphor, together with betel leaves.” Saying this, one should offer tāmbūla and then the honorarium with the mantra beginning “nākasya.”

column2: jayatyādīn paṭhan mantrān punar dhūpaṃ samarpayet | arcata ityādikān mantrān paṭhan nīrājayed dharim ||
column3: Reciting the mantras beginning “jayati,” one should offer incense again; reciting those beginning “arcata,” one should wave the light before Hari.

column2: puṣpāṇy aṣṭau samarpyātha mūlamantreṇa vaiṣṇavaḥ | vedamantraiś ca paurāṇair arpayet kusumāñjalim ||
column3: The Vaiṣṇava should then offer eight flowers with the root mantra and present a joined handful of flowers with Vedic and Purāṇic mantras.

column2: cāmaraṃ darpaṇaṃ chatraṃ vāhanādi nivedayet | mahārājopacārāṃś ca gītavāditranṛttakān | sarvān nivedayed bhaktyā mūlamantreṇa sādhakaḥ ||
column3: The practitioner should offer a fly-whisk, mirror, parasol, conveyance, and the other royal services, as well as song, instrumental music, and dance; all these should be devoutly presented with the root mantra.

column2: tataḥ śuddhena toyena śaṅkham āpūrya mudrikāḥ | dhenvādīḥ sampradarśyātha toyaṃ śaṅkhagataṃ spṛśet | aṣṭavāraṃ japen mūlaṃ bhrāmayet triḥ pradakṣiṇam ||
column3: Then one should fill the conch with pure water, display the Dhenu and other mudrās, touch the water in the conch, recite the root mantra eight times, and circle the conch clockwise three times.

column2: śaṅkhodakaṃ tu tatpātre sthāpayitvā pṛthak sudhīḥ | pradakṣiṇanamaskārān sūktapāṭhaṃ tataś caret ||
column3: The wise person should set the conch water separately in its vessel and then perform circumambulations, prostrations, and the recitation of hymns.

column2: āruhya vedikāṃ paścāt pūjāsādguṇyakārakam | mūlamantraṃ hariṃ dhyāyan japed aṣṭottaraṃ śatam ||
column3: After ascending the platform again, one should meditate upon Hari and recite the root mantra 108 times to make the worship complete in its excellence.

column2: ramābrahmādidevānāṃ dattvā tīrthādikaṃ balim | tattvanyāsān mātṛkāś ca punar mūrtau samācaret ||
column3: Having distributed sacred water and the other portions as offerings to Ramā, Brahmā, and the other deities, one should again perform upon the image the placements of the principles and of the Mother letters.

column2: punar dhyātvā hariṃ devam ātmā devety ṛcaṃ paṭhet | tata āvāhanīṃ mudrāṃ vyutkrameṇa vidhāya ca ||
column3: Meditating once more upon the divine Hari, one should recite the ṛk beginning “ātmā deva”; then one should perform the invocation mudrā in reverse order.

column2: ehy ehīti punaḥ procya punar āvāhayed dhṛdi | tathaiva parapūjāyāṃ ravyādau taṃ nidhāpayet ||
column3: Saying “come, come” once more, one should invoke Him back into the heart. In worship performed for another, one should similarly establish Him again in the sun or other original locus.

column2: yāce’haṃ tvā hṛṣīkeśa namāmi puruṣottama | hṛdi me kuru saṃvāsaṃ śriyā saha jagatpate ||
column3: “I beseech You, O Hṛṣīkeśa; I bow to You, O Supreme Person. O Lord of the universe, make Your dwelling in my heart together with Śrī.”

column2: iti prārthya hariṃ paścād vidadhyāt tattvamātṛkāḥ | dhyātvā samarpayed viṣṇuṃ yasya smṛtyeti mantrataḥ ||
column3: After praying to Hari in this way, one should perform the placements of the principles and Mother letters; then, meditating, one should dedicate everything to Viṣṇu with the mantra beginning “yasya smṛtyā.”

column2: tīrthaprasādagandhādīn dattvā viṣṇuparāya ca | tataḥ svayaṃ tu gṛhṇīyād bhaktyā natvā hariṃ smaran ||
column3: After giving the sacred water, prasāda, sandal paste, and the other gifts to one devoted to Viṣṇu, one should oneself receive them, bowing with devotion and remembering Hari.

column2: padyapāṭhe manuṣyāṇāṃ śramo nātibhaved iti | tantrasāroktapūjāyāṃ padyamāleyam īritā ||
column3: So that people may not experience excessive effort when reciting in verse, this Padyamālā has been composed for the worship prescribed in the Tantrasāra.

column2: anena bhagavān viṣṇuḥ prīto bhavati sarvadā | pramādato nirodhād vā hareḥ pūjā bhaven na cet | paṭhanāt padyamālāyā naraḥ pūjāphalaṃ labhet ||
column3: Through this, the Blessed Lord Viṣṇu is always pleased. If, because of inadvertence or an impediment, the worship of Hari cannot be performed, a person obtains the fruit of that worship by reciting the Padyamālā.

column2: iti śrījayatīrthākhyabhikṣuṇā racitā satī | tantrasāroktapūjānusāriṇī padyamālikā ||
column3: Thus ends the excellent Padyamālikā, composed by the ascetic known as Śrī Jayatīrtha and conforming to the worship taught in the Tantrasāra.

column2: iti śrījayatīrthaśrīcaraṇaviracitā śrīpadyamālā ||
column3: Thus ends the glorious Padyamālā composed by the venerable Śrī Jayatīrtha.

column2: śrīkṛṣṇārpaṇam astu ||
column3: May this be offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

column2: mukhyaprāṇavaśe sarvaṃ sa viṣṇor vaśagaḥ sadā | prīṇayāmo vāsudevaṃ devatāmaṇḍalākhaṇḍamaṇḍanam ||
column3: Everything is under the authority of Mukhya Prāṇa, and he is always subject to Viṣṇu. We propitiate Vāsudeva, the unbroken ornament of the entire assembly of deities.
